status.en: 13 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 63% more than the week before, most of them in La Espriella, Bogota and Cucuta.
status.nb: 13 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 63 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i La Espriella, Bogota og Cucuta.

summary.en: Hostile gunmen seized a supermarket in Cartagena, taking at least 20 hostages, while Colombian security forces surrounded the site and later freed all hostages. Simultaneously, a car bomb detonated in a central Colombian city, destroying buildings and injuring more than 20 people, and another car bomb hit the governor's office in Meta. The Colombian president blamed ex-FARC rebels for the car bomb blast. The ELN carried out a drone strike on a police base, injuring three people including an infant. Violence remains high, with 225 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Voldelige væpnede menn tok kontroll over et supermarked i Cartagena, og tok minst 20 gisler, mens colombianske sikkerhetsstyrker omringet stedet og senere frigjorde alle gislene. Samtidig detonerte en bilbombe i en sentral colombiansk by, ødela bygninger og såret mer enn 20 personer, og en annen bilbombe traff guvernørkontoret i Meta. Den colombianske presidenten la skylden på eks-FARC-opprørerne for bilbombeeksplosjonen. ELN utførte et droneredningsangrep på en politibase, og tre personer, inkludert et spedbarn, ble skadet. Voldnivået forblir høyt, med 225 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
